step_1_color.question: What is the bird's PRIMARY COLOR from aerial view?
step_1_color.help_text: Look at the dominant body color. This is the most reliable feature from high altitude.

options.label: WHITE/PALE
options.description: Pure white or very pale gray plumage (Pelicans, Egrets, Terns)

options.label: DARK/BLACK
options.description: Black, very dark brown, or dark gray (Cormorants, Anhingas, Skimmers, Noddies)

options.label: BLUE-GRAY
options.description: Blue-gray, slate, or ash colored (Herons, Night-Herons)

options.label: BROWN/REDDISH
options.description: Brown, reddish-brown, or mixed dark colors (Reddish Egret, Ibis, Gulls)

options.label: PINK/RED
options.description: Bright pink or reddish overall (Spoonbill - unmistakable!)

WHITE.question: What is the NECK LENGTH and BODY SIZE?
WHITE.help_text: Neck length is highly visible from aerial view - much more reliable than bill details!

options.label: VERY LONG NECK
options.description: Long elegant neck visible (Egrets, Herons, Stork)

options.label: SHORT NECK
options.description: Compact body with short neck (Terns, Avocet)

options.label: HUGE BODY
options.description: Massive body size, much larger than other birds (Pelican)

DARK.question: What is the NECK LENGTH and BODY SHAPE?
DARK.help_text: Neck is the key diagnostic feature - much easier to see than bill from above!

options.label: VERY LONG NECK
options.description: Long snake-like or S-curved neck (Cormorants, Anhinga)

options.label: SHORT NECK
options.description: Compact body, short neck (Terns, Skimmers, Gulls, Noddies)

options.label: VERY LONG WINGS
options.description: Extremely long pointed wings, forked tail (Frigatebird)

BLUE-GRAY.question: What is the NECK LENGTH?
BLUE-GRAY.help_text: Blue-gray herons separate cleanly by neck length from aerial view.

options.label: VERY LONG NECK
options.description: Extra-long neck, largest heron (Great Blue Heron)

options.label: LONG NECK
options.description: Long neck but smaller overall (Little Blue, Tricolored)

BROWN.question: What is the NECK LENGTH and BODY SHAPE?
BROWN.help_text: Brown birds separate well by neck length and body proportions.

options.label: MEDIUM NECK
options.description: Medium neck, wading bird shape (Ibis, Oystercatcher, Stilt)

PINK.question: CONFIRMATION - Roseate Spoonbill?
PINK.help_text: If it's pink, it's a Roseate Spoonbill. No other pink birds in this region!

options.label: YES - BRIGHT PINK
options.description: Bright pink with medium neck - UNMISTAKABLE!

species.name: Great Egret

species.name: Snowy Egret

species.name: Cattle Egret
species.confidence_tips: Stockiest egret, shortest neck of the white egrets

species.name: Wood Stork

species.name: White Egret (uncertain species)
key_features: Use when GREG vs SNEG vs CAEG uncertain
species.confidence_tips: Use when white egret species cannot be determined

WHITE_SHORT_NECK.question: Additional features for white short-necked birds:
WHITE_SHORT_NECK.help_text: Tern ID is challenging - use size and wing patterns. Avocet has distinctive posture.

species.name: Royal Tern
species.confidence_tips: Largest tern, orange bill if visible

species.name: Sandwich Tern
species.confidence_tips: Medium-sized tern with slender profile

species.name: Caspian Tern
species.confidence_tips: Heaviest tern, larger than ROYT

species.name: Least Tern
species.confidence_tips: Much smaller than all other terns - size is diagnostic

species.name: American Avocet
species.confidence_tips: Distinctive black/white wing pattern, elegant wader

species.name: Unidentified Tern

WHITE_HUGE_BODY.question: CONFIRMATION - American White Pelican?
WHITE_HUGE_BODY.help_text: Huge white bird - much larger than all other species.

species.name: American White Pelican
species.confidence_tips: Massive size is diagnostic - far larger than any egret

DARK_VERY_LONG_NECK.question: Key features for dark long-necked birds:
DARK_VERY_LONG_NECK.help_text: Anhinga has extremely long snake-like neck. Cormorants have S-curved necks.

species.name: Double-crested Cormorant
species.confidence_tips: Wing-spreading behavior is distinctive. Most common cormorant.

species.name: Neotropic Cormorant
species.confidence_tips: Smaller and more slender than DCCO - use location

species.name: Anhinga
species.confidence_tips: Snake-like neck is diagnostic - much longer than cormorants

species.name: Cormorant (species uncertain)
key_features: Use when DCCO vs NECO uncertain
species.confidence_tips: Use when cormorant species cannot be distinguished

DARK_SHORT_NECK.question: Key features for dark short-necked birds:
DARK_SHORT_NECK.help_text: Look at size, wing shape, and bill if visible. Skimmer has unique profile.

species.name: Black Skimmer

species.name: Black Tern

species.name: Brown Noddy

species.name: Laughing Gull

DARK_HUGE_BODY.question: CONFIRMATION - Brown Pelican?
DARK_HUGE_BODY.help_text: Massive dark bird - much larger than cormorants.

species.name: Brown Pelican
species.confidence_tips: Distinctive pelican size and shape - plunge dives

DARK_VERY_LONG_WINGS.question: CONFIRMATION - Magnificent Frigatebird?
DARK_VERY_LONG_WINGS.help_text: Extremely long wings and forked tail - unmistakable soaring silhouette.

species.name: Magnificent Frigatebird

BLUE-GRAY_VERY_LONG_NECK.question: CONFIRMATION - Great Blue Heron?

BROWN_LONG_NECK.question: CONFIRMATION - Reddish Egret?

species.name: Herring Gull

PINK_YES_BRIGHT_PINK.question: ROSEATE SPOONBILL - Final Confirmation
PINK_YES_BRIGHT_PINK.help_text: If you see pink, it's a Roseate Spoonbill. Period.

species.name: Roseate Spoonbill
species.confidence_tips: BRIGHT PINK! Cannot be confused with anything else in this region!

notes.major_change: Replaced BILL SHAPE with NECK LENGTH for Step 2. Bill details are too small to see reliably from aerial photographs, but neck length is highly visible and diagnostic.
rationale: Neck length is visible from high altitude aerial photography
Bill shape requires close-up views that aerial photos don't provide
This matches actual field identification practices for aerial surveys
Neck proportions are used by ornithologists for distant bird ID
notes.source: Based on Cornell Lab of Ornithology, Audubon Society, Gulf Coast avian monitoring protocols, and aerial survey methodology
accuracy_tips: COLOR is most reliable from aerial view - always start here
NECK LENGTH is the second-most visible feature from above
Long-necked birds (herons, egrets) are obvious even at distance
Short-necked birds (terns, gulls) have compact body profiles
Use colony context - species often segregate by habitat
Use relative comparison - if multiple birds visible, compare sizes and neck lengths
When uncertain, use combination codes (WHEG, UNCO, UNIB, etc.)
common_mistakes: Trying to identify bill details from aerial photos - use neck instead!
GREG vs SNEG - look at overall size and neck thickness
Cormorants vs Anhinga - Anhinga has distinctively longer snake-like neck
Night-herons vs other herons - night-herons have stocky bodies with short thick necks
Terns are very difficult from aerial view - use UNTE when uncertain
